html:
LuxLeaks was a 2014 leak of secret tax rulings that Luxembourg had granted to hundreds of large companies, which let them pay very little tax on profits routed through the country.

After steel declined, Luxembourg grew into a finance centre: banks, investment funds and holding companies drawn by low taxes and light rules. The documents, published by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, came from the accounting firm PwC.

The leak came just as Jean-Claude Juncker, long Luxembourg's prime minister, took over the European Commission. It led to new European rules requiring countries to share tax rulings. The whistleblowers were tried in Luxembourg, and the courts later recognised one of them as a whistleblower.
sum: LuxLeaks was a 2014 leak of secret tax rulings that Luxembourg had granted to hundreds of large companies, which let them pay very little tax on profits routed through the country.
